item.title: Joint Mideast peace efforts urged
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
The Middle East and the Gulf region should not become a wrestling arena for major-country rivalry or geopolitical conflicts, President Xi Jinping said on Monday, reiterating China's commitment to working with Arab states and countries of the Gulf Cooperation Council to strive for lasting peace in the region. Xi made the remarks during talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who was on a state visit to China from Sunday to Monday. This was the first visit to China by an Omani head of state since the two countries established diplomatic ties 48 years ago. Xi said that concerted efforts are needed by all parties to foster and safeguard peace and stability in the Middle East and the Gulf region. China has consistently been committed to ending hostility and promoting peace in the Middle East, and hopes to contribute wisdom and solutions to resolving the region's security dilemmas, he said. The nation will continue to advocate resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means and will support countries in the region in building a common homeland of good neighborliness, development, security and cooperation, Xi added. He expressed China's willingness to strengthen communication and coordination with Oman and other Arab and Gulf Cooperation Council countries to work together toward restoring peace and tranquility in the region and achieving lasting security and stability. The Omani sultan said that China plays an indispensable leading role in maintaining world peace and stability. Oman highly appreciates China's just stance on the Middle East issue and is willing to closely coordinate with China to uphold international law, advocate for the peaceful resolution of disputes, and jointly promote regional and global security and stability, he said. In a joint statement released on Monday on deepening the China-Oman strategic partnership, both countries expressed their encouragement for the United States and Iran to adhere to peaceful options, achieve a comprehensive ceasefire and cessation of hostilities as early as possible, and resume dialogue and negotiations to reach a comprehensive agreement that includes the nuclear issue. Both countries also maintain that the situation in the Strait of Hormuz should return to normal and safe navigation is restored, the statement said, and they agree to maintain communication on issues related to the strait. China has played a positive role on the Middle East issue. While meeting with Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, in Beijing in April, Xi put forward a four-point proposal on promoting peace and stability in the Middle East. He called for adhering to the principle of peaceful coexistence, the principle of national sovereignty, the principle of international rule of law, and a coordinated approach to development and security. On Monday, Foreign Minister Wang Yi met in Beijing with Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, emphasizing that dialogue and negotiation are the only viable solutions to the ongoing Middle East conflict. All parties should seek political resolution of the conflict in a rational and pragmatic spirit, rather than resorting to military confrontation, Wang said, adding that China will continue to work with all parties to restore peace in the region. Speaking at a regular news conference on Monday, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said that China will send its special envoy to the Middle East to visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month to implement the series of initiatives and proposals put forward by Xi on the Middle East issue. The visit aims to facilitate peace talks and ease tensions, and play a constructive role in maintaining regional peace and stability, she said. Bilateral cooperation During Monday's talks, the two heads of state pledged to promote bilateral ties. They witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents in areas such as Beidou Navigation Satellite System application, industrial and supply chains, green development, local currency swaps, digital payments and digital currency. Xi said that Sultan Haitham's visit will become an important chapter in the history of China-Oman relations, injecting strong momentum into the development of bilateral ties. He said that expanding and deepening China-Oman relations is a strategic choice for both sides, follows the trend of the times and historical development, and meets the common aspirations of the two peoples. China is committed to promoting high-quality development and expanding high-standard opening-up, which will bring greater opportunities to Oman and other countries worldwide, Xi said. He expressed China's willingness to deepen the synergy of development strategies with Oman and be a stable and reliable partner in the energy sector, a partner with promising potential in investment, and a partner in fostering innovation within advanced technologies. Sultan Haitham said that under the strong leadership of President Xi, China has become a major political and economic country in the world, making significant contributions to global prosperity and stability. Oman firmly adheres to the one-China principle and supports China in safeguarding its national sovereignty and territorial integrity, he said. He expressed hope to take this visit as a new starting point to explore more cooperation opportunities and build a future-oriented partnership. caodesheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Major zircon deposit found in Xinjiang
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
China has made a breakthrough in its mineral exploration efforts after a major zircon sand deposit was discovered in Baicheng county, Aksu prefecture, Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region. The Ministry of Natural Resources announced the discovery, with confirmed resources equivalent to those of more than 40 large zircon deposits and associated hafnium resources reaching a super-large scale, at a news conference in Beijing on Saturday. The discovery marks a major breakthrough in China's efforts to secure supplies of zircon, a mineral of which the country has relatively scarce resources. Around 70 percent of the world's zircon reserves are concentrated in Australia, while China accounts for less than 1 percent. The new find is expected to significantly strengthen the country's resource security. Zirconium, a silvery-gray transition metal, has a high melting point, excellent corrosion resistance and a low neutron absorption cross-section. These properties make it an important material for nuclear reactor fuel rod cladding and high-temperature alloys used in aerospace applications. Hafnium, which is commonly found alongside zirconium, has a high density and melting point. It is used in nuclear reactor control rods, rocket engines and spacecraft heat shields. Zhu Yilin, chief engineer of the Xinjiang department of natural resources, said the discovery was the culmination of nearly two decades of sustained exploration. Between 2006 and 2019, geologists reanalyzed historical geochemical survey data from the Tianshan region, and identified multiple zircon anomalies and promising exploration targets. According to Zhu, the regional government has allocated 35.19 million yuan ($5.28 million) to five zircon exploration projects since 2024, which led to the breakthrough following extensive fieldwork. "We will intensify exploration in promising zircon belts in Aksu, expand project deployment, strengthen metallogenic research and improve exploration technologies, with the aim of achieving further breakthroughs," Zhu said. He added that efforts would also be made to accelerate the transfer of mining rights through public bidding, encouraging rights holders to expand reserves and increase production. The discovery is among the major achievements of China's latest round of mineral exploration in the inaugural year of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-30). Other significant discoveries have also been made across the country. The discovery of a major copper-gold deposit in the Chating region of Xuancheng, Anhui province, was announced by the Ministry of Natural Resources in September. The exploration project completed nearly 100,000 meters of drilling in just four months. Meanwhile, Guizhou province reported the discovery of its first fully concealed, high-grade, thick and super-large lead-zinc deposit in Bijie. To gain a more comprehensive understanding of the country's mineral resources and strengthen resource security, the ministry has also launched a new round of resource reassessment during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, targeting associated and low-grade minerals, as well as strategic mineral resources that were previously difficult to exploit but may now be economically recoverable with advances in technology. limenghan@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Draft standard aiming to speed C-V2X rollout
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
A proposed mandatory national standard requiring commercial road transport in China to be fitted with cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) systems could accelerate the technology's rollout beyond pilot projects. The Ministry of Transport released the draft for public comment earlier this year. It is now under review after the comment period ended on Aug 29. Under the proposal, vehicles used in commercial road transport, other than trailers, would have to be equipped with systems using LTEV2X, a 4G-based form of C-V2X. The technology enables vehicles to exchange safety information directly with nearby vehicles and roadside infrastructure, supporting warnings about potential collisions and other road hazards. If adopted, the provision would turn C-V2X installation from a voluntary practice into a regulatory requirement for covered vehicles. Fan Ju, deputy general manager of CICT Connected and Intelligent Technologies, said C-V2X can warn drivers of hazards including rear-end collision risks, collision risks involving vehicles hidden from view by obstacles, and accidents ahead. Such functions can complement onboard cameras and radar, giving drivers or driver-assistance systems more time to respond, he said. Fan said the cost of installing C-V2X equipment during vehicle production is now relatively low. However, some automakers remain reluctant to adopt the technology because consumers may not perceive its benefits as readily as more visible features such as large infotainment screens. Deliveries of passenger vehicles fitted with C-V2X as standard equipment in China reached 344,000 in the first half, up 13.63 percent year-on-year, according to data from research institute Gaogong. In addition, C-V2X penetration in the passenger vehicle market stood at 4.03 percent. The proposal comes as China advances a vehicle-road-cloud integration pilot program launched by five government departments in 2024. The program covers 20 pilot areas, requires all participating vehicles to be equipped with C-V2X terminals and sets a 50 percent installation target for new vehicles in those areas. The pilot framework also calls for full 5G coverage in the pilot areas, connectivity for at least 90 percent of traffic signals and road signs, and LTE-V2X roadside communication units. Roadside sensing and edge-computing systems are to be deployed at key intersections and road sections. Figures published by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology in late 2025 put the number of intelligent roadside units deployed nationwide at more than 11,000. Automakers including FAW, SAIC, BYD and Nio have also launched production models equipped with C-V2X as standard. During the 2026 World Intelligent Connected Vehicles Conference in Beijing, vehicles from several automakers took part in a demonstration in which roadside sensors and communication networks alerted drivers and driver-assistance systems to pedestrians and cyclists obscured from view. Li Keqiang, an academician with the Chinese Academy of Engineering, said that 22 Chinese and foreign companies were taking part in a joint initiative to advance vehicle-road-cloud integration, up from 15 in 2025. The initiative also covered the development and testing of related functions on 21 models. Li said broader commercial cooperation is also taking shape, with 14 partnerships involving 26 companies across the automotive value chain, including automakers, companies involved in city-level vehicle networks and connected-vehicle component suppliers. He expects initial vehicle-road-cloud functions to be introduced in production vehicles by the end of 2026 and more closely integrated with driver-assistance systems in 2027. wangyuchen@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero makes a heroic debut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Following the phenomenal appearance of Black Myth: Wukong in 2024, the world recently witnessed the launch of another AAA-rated video game, Phantom Blade Zero, developed by a Chinese gaming company. Less than an hour after its release on Thursday, the game, developed by S-Game, had surpassed 300,000 concurrent players on Steam, a digital distribution platform for PC games, with the player count climbing to more than 720,000 at its peak later that day. In pre-release reviews, the PC version of Phantom Blade Zero earned an average score of 88 on the US review aggregator website Metacritic, surpassing the 81 scored by Black Myth: Wukong. On Steam, 88 percent of more than 33,250 Chinese-language users gave positive reviews, while the figure among English-language users also reached 88 percent. So far, the game has sold over 1 million copies, with preorder sales on the Steam and PS5 platforms estimated to surpass $43 million. US video game critic Travis Northup rated it 9 out of 10, praising the action role-playing game as "amazing". In his review on the US entertainment media platform Imagine Games Network, Northup wrote: "Phantom Blade Zero is an unbelievably smooth action game filled with memorable boss fights, compelling combat, and limitless swagger. … It is one of the best action games I've played in a long time." He added that "its tale of betrayal and revenge mostly plays it extremely safe, and some unfortunate invisible barriers and technical hiccups can cause minor frustrations — but the overwhelming majority of my time with this stunning, incredibly well-tuned adventure was downright awesome". The game begins with the story of a highly skilled martial artist named Soul, whose heart has been severely injured in a previous battle. On the verge of death, he is saved by a mysterious doctor. However, the treatment leaves him with only 66 days to live before his heart will ultimately fail. In the last days of his life, Soul embarks on a journey to find a new heart and to rediscover his true self and his original sense of chivalry in this dark phantom world full of lies and betrayals. It "truly captures the essence of the martial arts world in (prestigious Chinese writer) Gu Long's novels, which is dark, chaotic, brutal, and romantic", said Feng Ji, the producer of Black Myth: Wukong, in his WeChat Moments after watching the livestreaming of an actual gameplay preview in July. Before its official release, some 3 million people across all platforms added Phantom Blade Zero to their wish lists, making it one of the most anticipated Chinese action games of 2026. One of the reasons behind the game's popularity among foreign players lies in its rich kung fu elements. Liang Qiwei, or Soulframe Liang, founder of S-Game and the game's producer, said, "At its core, it's a story rich with traditional Chinese elements". Liang, 45, made his first game at Tsinghua University 21 years ago. In actual gameplay, what particularly impresses global players is the smooth, refreshing combat design in a style concept called "kungfupunk". "Kungfupunk" blends traditional elements of Chinese wuxia (a fiction genre centered on martial arts adventures in ancient China), an atmosphere of ancient jianghu, or the realm of martial arts, steampunk-style machinery, occult body modification, and a dark, rebellious punk spirit to create a new form of expression, Liang told media in an earlier interview. In this world, swordsmen, martial arts sects and old Chinese architecture coexist with mechanical limbs, grim industrial ruins and modern rock music. "We are creating an original global IP that belongs to us, strongly imprinted with the essence of Chinese wuxia culture," Liang said. The game offers a total of 30 different weapons, all inspired by the vast collection of traditional Chinese weaponry. "To understand how the weight and length of these weapons affect movement, we sometimes invite swordsmiths to forge them," Liang said in an article published online in April. The martial arts moves are captured from more than 20 highly experienced kung fu actors, including Hong Kong movie star Donnie Yen. Additionally, the production team explored locations like ancestral halls in Fujian province, ancient towns in Zhejiang province, and Beijing's old steel factories, scanning and creatively combining them into the unique "kungfupunk" art style.

item.title: South-South cooperation boon to world economy
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
The foundations for cooperation across countries and regions of the Global South are expanding. According to the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development, South-South merchandise exports rose from approximately $500 billion in 1995 to $6.8 trillion in 2025. More than half of developing countries' exports now go to other developing economies. At the same time, countries still differ significantly in their development conditions, industrial structures and ability to withstand external shocks. The key question is how to strengthen the development resilience of the Global South, or, how to translate its potential for cooperation into the capacity to drive shared development. The answers lie in the following areas. Respond to external shocks In the face of unilateralism and protectionism, the Global South should strengthen coordination and firmly uphold the multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core. We should safeguard basic principles such as most-favored-nation treatment and ensure that reforms respond more fully to the concerns of developing members. For small and medium-sized economies, predictable and nondiscriminatory rules are essential for businesses to gain fair access to international markets. Cooperation must respond to the practical needs of businesses. In my view, we can give priority to facilitating customs clearance, improving logistics connectivity and sharing market information. These efforts can help businesses find more trading partners and diversify their sources of supply. For essential products such as food and energy — which affect people's livelihoods — we should strengthen policy communication and reduce the impact of sudden policy changes on partner countries. A UN survey covering 174 economies in 2025 found that the global implementation rate for paperless trade measures was 72 percent, while the rate for cross-border paperless trade measures was 49 percent. When a trading partner accepts an electronic certificate of origin, a small or medium-sized business may save an administrative step and several days of waiting. Such practical improvements can gradually reduce the costs of doing business and boost overall trade. The Global South can begin with pilot projects at ports of entry and in sectors where conditions are suitable, expand their coverage as experience is gained and use technical assistance to help partners with more limited capacity participate. South-South cooperation should remain open and inclusive, with South-South and North-South cooperation reinforcing one another. By working with more partners and keeping trading channels open, countries can strengthen their ability to respond to external uncertainties and bring greater stability to the world economy. Improve industrial capabilities Shifts in industrial and supply chains have created opportunities for some countries in the Global South to attract investment and develop manufacturing. Once projects are in place, the sustainability of cooperation depends in part on how they generate local employment, develop skills and support local businesses. Openness to trade and investment and the development of local industries need to be supported by complementary policies. When attracting investment, countries can also improve power supplies and logistics, provide vocational training, and help local small and medium-sized enterprises meet quality and delivery standards. Local businesses can then gradually enter supply chains and share in the opportunities created by investment cooperation. The China-Egypt TEDA Suez Economic and Trade Cooperation Zone offers a practical example. By end-2025, the zone had attracted nearly 200 enterprises and more than $3.8 billion in actual investment, directly creating around 10,000 local jobs. High-voltage electrical equipment is manufactured locally in the zone, and products such as glass fiber are sold in international markets. The zone demonstrates how industrial cooperation can create a positive link between cross-border investment and stronger local manufacturing capabilities. Every country has a legitimate interest in developing its own industries. Industrial policy should reflect national conditions, respect multilateral rules, and emphasize transparency and effective implementation. Industries at an early stage of development can receive appropriate support within the limits allowed by established rules. Such support should be accompanied by mechanisms for evaluation and adjustment, with more resources directed toward infrastructure, technological research and development, and workers' skills. Cooperation projects should also fully respect host countries' development plans and take into account environmental protection, workers' interests and the interests of local communities. Cooperation has a sound foundation when businesses are willing to invest for the long term and local communities receive tangible benefits. Furthermore, equipment needs people to maintain it once it is in use, and production lines need people to manage them once they are built. Universities, vocational colleges and businesses can jointly develop training programs so that industrial cooperation and talent development advance together. Ultimately, industrial development should strengthen local capabilities. Enhance financial cooperation Financial market volatility affects trade and investment through exchange rates, interest rates and capital flows. In strengthening financial cooperation, the Global South should focus on real trade and project needs and improve arrangements for settlement, financing and risk management. For trade settlement, countries can steadily expand the use of local currencies in line with market demand and businesses' voluntary participation, while improving direct currency conversion, clearing and supporting financing services. In 2025, the central banks of Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand harmonized and broadened the operational rules of the Local Currency Transaction Framework, providing a more coordinated framework for cross-border trade and investment. This experience merits study in light of each country's circumstances. Local currency settlement can reduce some of the costs of converting through an intermediate currency. Better matching the currencies in which businesses receive income and make payments can also help them manage exchange rate risks. Exchange rates between currencies still fluctuate, and the actual benefits depend on market liquidity, financing costs and the availability of hedging tools. We should therefore give businesses greater convenience and choice, backed by appropriate financial services. For long-term investment, multilateral development institutions such as the Shanghai-based New Development Bank can help expand local currency financing and co-financing. In 2023, the NDB issued its first bonds in South Africa, totaling 1.5 billion rand ($90.25 million). It announced that the proceeds would be used for infrastructure and sustainable development projects in South Africa. This offers a practical way to raise funds in local capital markets and support local development. For projects that earn most of their revenue in local currency, appropriate use of local currency financing can reduce the risks arising from a mismatch between the currencies of revenue and debt service. Project cash flows, debt servicing capacity, and construction and operating conditions must also be assessed, with loan maturities set accordingly. Sound projects are the basis for lasting financial cooperation. Countries can also strengthen communication among central banks and regulatory authorities and improve currency swap, liquidity support and risk information-sharing arrangements suited to their circumstances. Regional cooperation should complement the global financial safety net, helping businesses that are operating normally continue their trade and investment activities during periods of market volatility. By making trade flows smoother, ensuring that industrial cooperation strengthens local capabilities and aligning financing more closely with the needs of the real economy, we can gradually improve our collective ability to respond to external shocks. We can also contribute to a fairer, more open and inclusive international economic order. The writer is a professor of the University of International Business and Economics. The views do not necessarily reflect those of China Daily.

item.title: China's Defense Ministry criticizes Japanese drama VIVANT
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
On Nov 1, China's Ministry of National Defense released a video titled Who's Turning History Upside Down?, criticizing the second season of the Japanese spy thriller VIVANT for deliberately twisting the facts and depicting "Chinese operatives" using torture methods employed by Japanese invaders against Chinese resistance fighters, in an attempt to whitewash Japan's history of aggression.

item.title: Yan An in Yan'an: Rediscovering the spirit of Nanniwan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
"Who wouldn't want a tractor of their own?" This unexpected remark from China Daily reporter Yan An may leave you wondering. As the 90th anniversary of the Long March (1934-36) is marked this year, Yan An returns to Yan'an, the final destination of the Long March and a city whose name shares the pronunciation of her own, to explore how the spirit of the Long March continues to inspire young people today. This time, she revisits Nanniwan, once hailed as the "Jiangnan of northern Shaanxi". Today, Nanniwan is not only taking on a new look but is also being transformed by a new generation of farmers. Meet Ma Qiang, a Party member born in the 1990s who returned to his hometown to start an agricultural business. With modern farming machinery, he helps local villagers work more efficiently, boost agricultural output and increase their incomes through the farmers' cooperative. Join Yan An in the cradle of the Chinese revolution and discover how modernization is bringing new life to this historic land.

item.title: Portugal-China chamber official on China's success
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Bernardo Mendia, secretary-general of the Portugal-China Chamber of Commerce and Industry, recently told China Daily's Global Lens that long-term planning, and a governance system that promotes officials based on proven performance are key to China's development. Long-term planning, he said, underpins stability and predictability — for investors and for the country itself. He called long-term planning China's "secret sauce" — the factor that has taken China from 1978 to becoming the world's second-largest economy. He added that a stable China with a long-term vision is injecting stability into an unstable world. (Reporter: Luan Ruiying, Video: Pan Yixuan, Intern: Gao Jiayi)
